findings.issue: The bot ban on advice/golden is anchored at `golden$`, so `import { parseGoldenSpots } from '../advice/golden.js'` (and '.ts') in src/bots passes lint. Under moduleResolution 'bundler', tsc resolves '.js' to golden.ts, so this is a working bypass of SPEC-04 / D-3. The engine patterns don't have this hole because their negative lookahead rejects 'hand.js'.
findings.evidence: In-process ESLint with the repo config: src/bots/p.ts `import { parseGoldenSpots } from '../advice/golden.js'` -> 0 errors; same with '.ts' -> 0 errors; '../advice/golden' -> no-restricted-imports error. A scratch tsc project (bundler resolution) compiles `from '../advice/golden.js'` with exit 0.
findings.fix: Change the regex to `(^|/)advice/golden(\.[cm]?[jt]sx?)?$` (or `(^|/)advice/golden(\.|$)`), and add a `../advice/golden.js` probe to the SPEC-04 sandbox run.

findings.issue: ADVICE_BOUNDARY_PATTERNS doesn't stop a bot-reachable advice file from importing './golden'. golden.ts is exempt from the advice block, so e.g. recommend.ts could `import { parseGoldenSpots } from './golden'` and re-export it, and bots would reach golden's createHand/applyAction path through advice. That undoes the SPEC-04 ban and the D-3 aim of keeping hand-state code out of the advice code bots can reach. The spec's tables don't list this case, but it is the transitive form of the exact drift §3 names ('a bot importing advice/golden'). No advice module imports golden today, so the ban costs nothing.
findings.evidence: In-process lint: src/advice/p.ts `import { parseGoldenSpots } from './golden'; export { parseGoldenSpots };` -> 0 errors. `grep -rn golden src` finds no src import of golden.
findings.fix: Add `{ regex: '(^|/)golden(\.[cm]?[jt]sx?)?$', message: ADVICE_BOUNDARY_MESSAGE }` (or a `(^|/)advice/golden` / `^\./golden` form) to ADVICE_BOUNDARY_PATTERNS, plus one sandbox probe such as src/advice/probe-golden.ts. If the orchestrator decides this is out of spec, record it as a follow-up task instead.

findings.issue: BOT_TYPE_IMPORT_SYNTAX covers only engine paths, so `export type G = import('../advice/golden').GoldenSpot` and `typeof import('../advice/golden')` pass in src/bots, while `import type { GoldenSpot } from '../advice/golden'` fails. This is a compile-time-only gap with no runtime reach, but it is the same kind of import()/import-type mismatch this task closes for the engine.
findings.evidence: In-process lint: src/bots/p.ts `export type H = import('../advice/golden').GoldenSpot;` -> 0 errors.
findings.fix: Add `TSImportType[source.value=/(^|\/)advice\/golden(\.|$)/]` to the first BOT_TYPE_IMPORT_SYNTAX selector.

findings.issue: No probe covers the non-normalized-path pattern in ADVICE_BOUNDARY_PATTERNS (first entry). It is the only entry that catches `import { createHand } from '../engine/./hand'` in advice (the other engine patterns need 'engine/<name>' with no further slash), so deleting it would open a bypass and every test would still pass. The same holds for the non-normalized half of the first BOT_TYPE_IMPORT_SYNTAX selector, although for type imports it is redundant with the other selectors.
findings.evidence: ADVICE_PROBES has create-hand, hand-state, view-fn and deck. None uses '/./', '//' or 'name/..'.

findings.issue: Advice `import '../engine/hand';` passes, because allowImportNames ignores imports with no specifiers. The bot block adds BOT_SIDE_EFFECT_IMPORT for exactly this reason. No bindings are imported, so there is no data access.
findings.fix: Optional: give adviceHiddenStateConfig a no-restricted-syntax side-effect selector. Note that this replaces the headless block's no-restricted-syntax options for src/advice, so the headless entries would have to be repeated. That cost probably outweighs the benefit, so leaving it as is is acceptable.

summary: SPEC-01..03 and 05..08 are implemented as specified and verified: 50 in-process bypass probes; the new test file passes; git diff vs main for src and the locked test is empty; decision-3 exists. The TSImportType selectors catch HandState, typeof-module, typeof createHand, dotted qualifiers, .ts/.js extensions, '/./', '//', 'x/..', './..' and nested folders, and allowed PlayerView/Action/SeatNumber/Street/advice types still pass. The advice block catches named, type, inline-type, default, namespace, export-from, export-star and mixed imports of hand state. Removing any engine selector or pattern fails at least one test, except the advice non-normalized pattern. Two MAJOR gaps in the golden ban: bots can import '../advice/golden.js', which tsc resolves under bundler resolution, and bot-reachable advice files can import './golden' and re-export it.
